blurb: Week 0 is the first day of your last period. There is no baby yet — dating starts here because it is the one date that can be pinned down reliably.
Still counting from your last period. Ovulation is roughly a fortnight away.
Ovulation happens around now. Conception, when it happens, is usually dated to this week.
A fertilised egg is dividing as it travels to the uterus and implants. Far too small to see.
Implantation is complete and the pregnancy hormone hCG starts rising — this is when a test usually turns positive.
The neural tube, which becomes the brain and spinal cord, is forming. The heart is a simple tube that has just begun to beat.
Facial features start as small folds. Arm and leg buds appear. A heartbeat may be visible on an early scan.
The brain is growing fast. Hands and feet look like paddles. The umbilical cord is fully formed.
All the essential organs have begun to form. Fingers and toes are webbed but distinct.
The embryo is officially a fetus this week. Tiny muscles allow the first movements, far too faint to feel.
Vital organs are in place and starting to work. Nails begin forming and bones are hardening.
The head is still about half the total length. Tooth buds are appearing and fingers and toes have separated.
Reflexes are developing — fingers can curl. The 12-week dating scan usually happens around now.
Start of the second trimester. Vocal cords are forming and fingerprints have appeared.
The baby can squint, frown and grimace. Fine downy hair called lanugo covers the body.
Bones are hardening quickly. The baby can sense light through closed eyelids.
Facial muscles allow expressions. The heart pumps around 25 litres of blood a day.
Fat stores begin forming under the skin. The skeleton is shifting from cartilage to bone.
Hearing is developing — the baby may start to register sounds. Many people feel the first movements around now.
A waxy coating called vernix now protects the skin. The senses are developing rapidly.
Halfway. The anomaly scan usually happens this week. From next week length is measured crown to heel, so the number jumps.
Measurement switches to full length, crown to heel. The baby swallows small amounts of amniotic fluid daily.
Eyebrows and eyelashes are visible. Grip is developing and the sense of touch is sharpening.
Hearing is good enough to pick up your voice. Skin is still wrinkled while fat fills out underneath.
A milestone week: lungs are developing the branches needed to breathe air.
The baby is putting on fat steadily. Hair is growing and beginning to show colour and texture.
Eyes open for the first time. Lungs are practising breathing movements with amniotic fluid.
End of the second trimester. Sleeping and waking patterns are becoming regular and hiccups are common.
Third trimester. The brain is developing deep grooves and the baby can now dream.
Muscles and lungs are maturing. Kicks are getting noticeably stronger.
Around a litre and a half of amniotic fluid surrounds the baby — this begins to reduce as space runs short.
All five senses are working. The baby is putting on weight quickly now.
Fingernails and toenails have grown in. Most babies have turned head-down or will soon.
Skull bones stay soft and separate to make the journey out easier. The immune system is developing.
Fat continues to fill out under the skin. Lungs are nearly ready.
The brain gains weight rapidly. Space is tight, so movements feel more like rolls than kicks.
The baby is likely head-down and settling into position. Weight gain is around 30g a day.
Early term. The baby practises breathing, sucking and blinking, getting ready for the outside.
Organs are mature and ready. The vernix and lanugo are mostly shed.
Full term. The chest is becoming more prominent and the head is roughly the size of the chest.
Your due date. Only about 4 in 100 babies arrive on it — anywhere from 37 to 42 weeks is normal.
